Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings:
• Single suspected wasp/bee sting a few minutes prior to consult  
• Localized erythema at puncture site; no visible swelling, no respiratory compromise on video exam  
• Subjective mild dyspnoea and lip tingling; anxiety present  
• Past history: eczema; penicillin allergy; no prior anaphylaxis

Working diagnosis:
• Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (uncomplicated venom-induced inflammation) — high likelihood per transcript and DDx.

Considerations:
• Early IgE-mediated anaphylaxis (medium likelihood; monitor for progression—lip/tongue swelling, stridor, respiratory distress).  
• Anxiety/panic reaction contributing to perceived dyspnoea (medium likelihood).

Management:
• Educate on red-flag symptoms of anaphylaxis; advise urgent ED attendance if breathing difficulty, lip/tongue swelling, or stridor develops.  
• Commence OTC antihistamine (e.g., Chlorphenamine 4 mg up to 6 ×/day or non-sedating once-daily alternative).  
• Monitor sting site; return if spreading erythema, heat, or systemic signs suggesting cellulitis (low likelihood).  
• Provide patient information link on anaphylaxis.  
• No immediate need for allergy testing or EpiPen; reconsider if recurrent reactions.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

1. Localized allergic reaction to insect sting – High likelihood: matches isolated cutaneous findings without systemic compromise.  
2. Early IgE-mediated anaphylaxis – Medium likelihood: timing and subjective lip/tongue symptoms warrant caution despite normal exam.  
3. Anxiety/panic attack – Medium likelihood: history of anxiety and disproportionate dyspnoea in absence of objective signs.
